facts.text: Westchester Square traces its roots to 1654 when Thomas Pell negotiated a land purchase from the Siwanoy Lenape people.
The 6 train’s Westchester Square–East Tremont Avenue station anchors the neighborhood as a transit gateway linking to Manhattan.
Westchester Creek and nearby parks have been reclaimed, restoring a waterfront identity that echoes the neighborhood’s colonial origins.
The Huntington Free Library, a non‑circulating private library at 9 Westchester Square, houses a rich collection of local history.
The historic Square Theater and long‑running family businesses have kept a sense of continuity amid new Latin American and Caribbean eateries.
The neighborhood’s central park, once called Westchester Playground, was renamed The Pearly Gates in 1998 by Parks Commissioner Henry Stern.
